thread.subject: Quick question about the Make x OpenAI hackathon
thread.body:
Hey Julius,

Congrats on the Make x OpenAI hackathon on Jan 16 — the focus on real use cases over presentations is exactly what the space needs. I saw revel8 is a partner alongside OpenAI and Make, which sounds like a solid lineup.

One thing I’m curious about: how are you planning to showcase revel8’s AI simulations within the challenge itself? Is it more of a tool participants can build on, or a separate track?

Best, Lena

thread.subject: Re: Make x OpenAI Hackathon — revel8 showcase
thread.body:
Hi Julius,

Good question — I’m Lena, community lead at hackathon-connect.io. We’re a small matchmaking platform that helps organizers and partners surface integration opportunities for events like this one. I saw revel8 listed on the public Make x OpenAI hackathon partner page (the one with OpenAI, Make, Zauber, Knowunity, Qontext, telli, Celonis, OSM) — that’s where I pulled it from.

My role is just to gather a few quick notes from partners for a roundup we’re publishing for participating teams — nothing official, no internal docs. Totally get you wanting to verify first.

If it’s easier, I can send you the exact public URL — but since you’re already on the partner list, maybe you can just confirm: is revel8’s simulation engine something teams will get hands-on access to during the challenge, or is it more of a judging/use-case showcase?

Also — I’ve put together a short “Files Review” page for partners to drop in any public one-liners or links they want teams to see. It’s password-protected, but you can sign in with your work email and it takes 30 seconds. Want me to send you the invite link?

Best, Lena

thread.subject: Quick question on your AI Course Builder post
thread.body:
Hi Tom,

Saw your post about the AI Course Builder update — the part about turning policies into interactive modules really stood out. I’m curious how you’re handling the compliance side when different roles need different levels of depth.

Do you find the triggered campaigns help with that, or is it more about the content customization?

Best, Lena

Lena Hartwig
thread.reply:
Hi Lena,

Thanks for writing. Which company are you with, and what is your role? Are you looking at this as a customer, a researcher or something else? Which post do you mean? Then I can answer properly. In short, role-based depth is mostly a content and targeting question, and triggered campaigns only help when they mirror the person's real role.

Best,
Tom

thread.subject: Re: AI Course Builder
thread.body:
Hi Tom,

Fair questions. I’m a compliance analyst at a mid-sized logistics firm — we’re evaluating training platforms, and your Academy is on the shortlist. The post I mean was the one on LinkedIn about the AI Course Builder’s policy-to-module workflow.

To be concrete: we have drivers, warehouse leads, and office staff, all needing different policy depth. If I upload a policy, can I set role-based depth per module, or is that only via separate campaigns? And roughly — how many triggered campaigns do you see a typical customer run per policy?

Best, Lena

Lena Hartwig
thread.reply:
Hi Lena,

Thanks. Role-based depth is set per module through content variants and audience targeting, not only via separate campaigns. For a detailed walkthrough and numbers, please book a demo through the revel8 website, where our sales team will pick it up. I don't share typical campaign counts by email. Also, I won't open the Files Review link. If you want to send material, please use your company address.

Best,
Tom
